architecture_decisions.recommendation: Removed duplicate dialog components (document-delete-dialog, document-duplicate-dialog, template-delete-dialog, template-duplicate-dialog) and consolidated functionality into envelope-delete-dialog and envelope-duplicate-dialog components
architecture_decisions.rationale: The envelope abstraction already existed in the codebase (EnvelopeType enum with DOCUMENT and TEMPLATE values). By consolidating duplicate components, we reduce code duplication, simplify maintenance, and ensure consistent behavior across document and template operations. The envelope components were already designed to handle both types through the `type` prop.
alternatives_considered: Keeping separate components for documents and templates
Creating a single generic dialog with conditional rendering
Using higher-order components to wrap type-specific logic

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated envelope dialogs to use envelope-specific tRPC mutations (envelope.delete and envelope.duplicate) instead of document/template-specific mutations
architecture_decisions.rationale: The backend already had envelope-level mutations that could handle both document and template operations. This aligns with the frontend consolidation and ensures a single source of truth for envelope operations. The envelope mutations accept an envelopeId and handle type-specific logic server-side.
alternatives_considered: Keeping separate document.delete and template.deleteTemplate mutations
Creating a new unified mutation endpoint
Using conditional client-side routing to different mutations

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Fixed share dialog auto-closing issue by adding DO_NOT_INVALIDATE_QUERY_ON_MUTATION to the share mutation and improving dialog content styling
architecture_decisions.rationale: The share dialog was closing because tRPC query invalidation was causing component re-renders. By preventing automatic query invalidation on the share mutation, we maintain the dialog state. Additionally, improved the title styling with better text wrapping to handle long document titles.
alternatives_considered: Managing dialog state locally without tRPC state changes
Using a different state management approach for share links

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated end-to-end tests to reflect new toast messages and dialog behavior after consolidation
architecture_decisions.rationale: Test assertions needed to be updated because toast messages changed from 'Envelope Duplicated' to type-specific messages ('Document Duplicated' or 'Template Duplicated'). This ensures tests accurately reflect user-facing text changes and maintain test reliability.
alternatives_considered: Keeping old test assertions and updating toast messages to match
Creating generic toast messages that work for both document and template

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated dropdown components to use the new envelope dialogs with proper trigger integration using DropdownMenuItem asChild pattern
architecture_decisions.rationale: Dropdown menu items need to trigger dialogs while maintaining proper accessibility and event handling. The asChild pattern allows the dialog trigger to be rendered as a child of DropdownMenuItem, ensuring proper menu behavior while enabling dialog functionality. This maintains the existing dropdown UX while switching to consolidated dialogs.
alternatives_considered: Creating separate dialog trigger buttons outside dropdowns
Using imperative dialog opening via refs
Redesigning the entire dropdown-dialog interaction pattern

implementation_summary:
The implementation consolidates duplicate dialog components by leveraging the existing envelope abstraction in the codebase. Instead of maintaining separate delete and duplicate dialogs for documents and templates, we now use unified envelope-delete-dialog and envelope-duplicate-dialog components that handle both types through the EnvelopeType enum (DOCUMENT or TEMPLATE). This reduces code duplication from 6 dialog components down to 2, simplifying maintenance and ensuring consistent behavior.

The envelope dialogs were enhanced to provide type-specific messaging and behavior. For example, the delete dialog now shows 'Document deleted' vs 'Template deleted' based on the envelope type, and similar adjustments were made for duplicate operations. All dropdown components that previously used the old dialogs were updated to use the new envelope dialogs with proper trigger integration using the asChild pattern for DropdownMenuItem components.

A critical fix was also implemented for the share dialog auto-closing issue. The problem was caused by tRPC query invalidation triggering component re-renders. By adding DO_NOT_INVALIDATE_QUERY_ON_MUTATION to the share mutation configuration, we prevent automatic query invalidation that was causing the dialog to close. Additionally, the share dialog title styling was improved with better text wrapping to handle long document titles. End-to-end tests were updated to reflect the new toast messages, ensuring test reliability matches the new user-facing text.
